title: Local Consistency Does Not Guarantee Global Conservation: Auditing Zero-Shot Composition of Airway Flow Operators

paper.title:
Local Consistency Does Not Guarantee Global Conservation:
Auditing Zero-Shot Composition of Airway Flow Operators
paper.abstract:
Abstract Neural operators approximate PDE solutions within a geometry family, but
independently learned local operators need not form a consistent global
simulator. We study frozen, single-pass composition for steady incompressible
flow in idealized two-dimensional airway trees. Separate Tube, bifurcation,
and trifurcation DeepONets are trained on 4,872 primitive CFD cases using field
supervision and auxiliary divergence, port-flux, component-balance, and
port-pressure penalties. The validation-selected deployment is frozen before
whole-tree CFD fields are inspected and assembled without tree training,
iterative coupling, flux correction, or CFD-informed adjustment. It retains
major flow patterns and controlled pathology responses with 0.204 0.204 – 0.215 0.215 s CPU inference, but has a 22.68 % 22.68\% prescribed-inlet-normalized external residual. A post-hoc sensitivity protocol,
frozen before new training and evaluation, repeats Data, Div, and Full models
across three seeds with Tube fixed. Relative to Data, Full reduces primitive
composite scores by 26.7 % 26.7\% for Y2 and 26.4 % 26.4\% for Y3 and reduces
assembled component-residual and interface-mismatch RMS by 7.2 % 7.2\% and 16.6 % 16.6\% .
Nevertheless, mean tree velocity error increases by 7.5 % 7.5\% , and external
residual increases from 17.49 ± 4.38 % 17.49\pm 4.38\% to 26.77 ± 3.65 % 26.77\pm 3.65\% .
Local regularization can therefore improve primitive and assembled-local
diagnostics without ensuring accurate global fields or conservation.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: High-fidelity numerical simulation is essential for analysing flow and transport in complex branching systems, but repeatedly solving geometrically detailed domains can be computationally expensive. Learned surrogates amortize this cost by mapping geometries and operating parameters to solution fields. A full-domain surrogate, however, must cover the distribution of complete configurations encountered at inference and offers limited reuse when similar local structures recur across systems. This motivates our central question: can operators learned independently on reusable physical primitives be frozen and composed into an unseen larger system without full-domain retraining? Neural operators provide a natural framework for this question. Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets), Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs), and physics-informed DeepONets learn mappings between input functions or parameterized physical configurations and their solution fields [ 11 , 9 , 15 ] . Geometry-aware extensions such as GINO accommodate varying irregular geometries, but still predict a solution over each complete computational domain [ 10 ] . Generalization across full-domain geometries is therefore distinct from independently learning local component operators and assembling them into a previously unseen hierarchy: the latter additionally requires predictions from different operators to be mutually compatible at their interfaces. Physics-informed objectives can improve local fidelity by incorporating differential-equation residuals, boundary conditions, conservation penalties, and interface or flux constraints [ 15 , 7 ] . These constraints act within the domains on which they are imposed, whereas composition introduces additional system-level requirements. Consequently, low field and physics errors on isolated primitives do not imply a consistent assembled solution: local field accuracy ⇏ globally consistent composition . \text{local field accuracy}\;\not\Rightarrow\;\text{globally consistent composition}. (1) In an incompressible branching system, small component residuals can coexist with parent–child flux mismatches, incompatible pressure gauges, or errors that accumulate across successive generations. Classical Schwarz methods obtain global consistency through iterative transmission of interface information [ 3 ] . Recent learned local-to-global solvers retain explicit coupling: Schwarz Neural Inference and Neural-Schwarz Tiling repeatedly update predictions over overlapping subdomains [ 6 , 14 ] , while CoMLSim combines local representations with iterative inference [ 13 ] . M2PDE instead generates coupled multiphysics or multi-component solutions by sampling from a joint generative model [ 17 ] . We study a deliberately stricter regime: independently trained operators are frozen and evaluated once, then assembled without iterative exchange, joint generation, flux correction, or global projection. The contribution is therefore a controlled composition audit, rather than a converged learned domain-decomposition solver. We investigate this regime using steady two-dimensional airway flow. Airway trees are organized as multigeneration tubular segments connected by branching junctions [ 5 , 8 ] . Following the reusable primitive abstraction developed in RespGeomLib [ 16 ] , we represent these structures as Tube, bifurcation (Y2), and trifurcation (Y3) components, here idealized in two dimensions to permit controlled auditing of component and interface errors. This setting preserves nontrivial velocity, pressure, resistance, and interface physics while allowing component and connection errors to be audited separately. The study is not a patient-specific respiratory model and does not claim unrestricted topology generalization or prediction of physiological terminal-flow redistribution. Here, zero-shot field composition is conditional on a predeclared terminal-flow allocation. Before any monolithic solution field is accessed, each component inflow is obtained from the sum of its descendant terminal flows and determines its parabolic inlet-speed scale; resistance inputs follow the training-row matching rule documented in Appendix A.4 . No assembled tree enters training, validation, selection, or correction, and Selected predictions are frozen before monolithic CFD velocity and pressure fields are inspected. The post-hoc sensitivity audit reuses primitive-selected checkpoints without tree-based selection. We contribute a controlled audit of frozen, single-pass operator composition. The primary validation-selected deployment is archived before whole-tree CFD fields are inspected. A subsequent sensitivity protocol, frozen before new training and evaluation, repeats Data, Div, and Full branching operators over three seeds while holding Tube fixed. The resulting audit separates primitive consistency, assembled component and interface discrepancies, and the external boundary budget. It shows that improvements in the first two levels do not ensure improved global fields or conservation.

sections.heading: Evaluation protocol.
sections.text: The Selected primitive checkpoints and tree arrays constitute the primary prediction-before-CFD-field-inspection evaluation. The Data/Div/Full comparisons are post-hoc after unblinding. Before training seeds 2027 and 2028, we froze their configurations, seeds, checkpoint-selection rule, evaluation order, and output locations. We then evaluated all 18 primitive checkpoints and all 27 matched-seed tree deployments without result-based substitution. Seed-2026 tree outputs reproduce the previous post-hoc arrays bitwise. All seed summaries are computed from individual runs and report mean ± \pm sample SD; the three controlled tree conditions are not treated as statistical replicates.

sections.heading: Three-seed tree sensitivity.
sections.text: Full lowers the case-averaged component-residual and interface-mismatch RMS relative to Data in each of the three seeds; their mean reductions are 7.2 % 7.2\% and 16.6 % 16.6\% . Mean vector and speed Rel L 2 L_{2} increase by 7.5 % 7.5\% and 2.4 % 2.4\% , while pressure Rel L 2 L_{2} decreases by only 0.9 % 0.9\% . External residual increases from 17.49 ± 4.38 % 17.49\pm 4.38\% for Data to 26.77 ± 3.65 % 26.77\pm 3.65\% for Full and is higher for Full in every seed. Div reaches 33.75 ± 8.74 % 33.75\pm 8.74\% . Thus, improved primitive and assembled-local diagnostics do not guarantee improved global fields or external conservation.

sections.heading: Pathology attribution.
sections.text: Within each variant-seed, the condition-invariant external residual measures the external-port budget by telescoping and cannot localize internal error; signed attribution is in Appendix A.6 .

sections.heading: 4 Limitations
sections.text: This non-clinical study treats steady laminar flow in idealized 2D rigid-wall airways, excluding patient anatomy, unsteadiness, wall motion, and turbulence. One topology with prescribed inputs and terminal flows is tested, not arbitrary topologies or physiological redistribution. Selected is one validation-fixed seed-2026 blend. The three-seed Data/Div/Full protocol was frozen before new training and evaluation but after original primitive-test and whole-tree CFD unblinding; n = 3 n=3 gives descriptive, not inferential, variability. Pathology conditions are not independent replicates. The external residual telescopes to the external-port budget and cannot localize error; the assembler enforces neither interface-flux continuity nor global balance. Unmatched hardware precludes a normalized speedup claim.

sections.heading: 5 Conclusion
sections.text: Across three seeds, auxiliary objectives improve primitive composite scores and divergence, while Full reduces assembled component-residual and interface-mismatch RMS. Yet Full raises mean external residual from 17.49 % 17.49\% to 26.77 % 26.77\% ; such gains do not ensure lower whole-tree field error or imbalance. Frozen primitive operators are useful diagnostics, but reliable composition requires conservative interface coupling, global projection, or iterative correction rather than local regularization alone.

sections.heading: Broader impacts.
sections.text: Faster reusable flow surrogates could reduce the computational cost of exploratory scientific simulation. However, the present model is not clinically validated, and its pressure and conservation errors could lead to unsafe conclusions if used for diagnosis, treatment planning, or device design without independent CFD or experimental verification.

sections.heading: Field sampling and normalization.
sections.text: Every prepared case stores 1,024 field points. Legacy cases retain their frozen prepared samples. Pilot points are sampled deterministically and uniformly with respect to triangle area, followed by P 1 P_{1} interpolation of the CFD fields. At each training epoch, 256 stored field points are randomly selected per case, and 64 points are selected independently for divergence. Frozen primitive-test evaluation uses all 1,024 field points and 256 divergence points per case. Branch-feature normalization uses population means and standard deviations fitted across training cases only. Target-channel population means and standard deviations are fitted across all 1,024 spatial samples of the training cases only. The same training-fitted statistics are applied without refitting to validation and test cases.

sections.heading: Port supervision.
sections.text: Only pilot branch cases provide port supervision: Y2 has 180 supervised cases split 132/24/24, Y3 has 144 split 96/24/24, and Tube has none. Legacy Y2/Y3 port losses are masked because exact port geometry is unavailable. Primitive supervision uses 32-point fixed-order arclength midpoint quadrature on tagged, mesh-realized CFD caps. Whole-tree inference instead uses 32-point Gauss–Legendre quadrature on exact analytic interfaces; these are distinct quadrature procedures.

We study frozen, single-pass composition for steady incompressible flow in idealized two-dimensional airway trees. Separate Tube, bifurcation, and trifurcation DeepONets are trained on 4,872 primitive CFD cases using field supervision and auxiliary divergence, port-flux, component-balance, and port-pressure penalties. The validation-selected deployment is frozen before whole-tree CFD fields are inspected and assembled without tree training, iterative coupling, flux correction, or CFD-informed adjustment. It retains major flow patterns and controlled pathology responses with 0.204 0.204 – 0.215 0.215 s CPU inference, but has a 22.68 % 22.68\% prescribed-inlet-normalized external residual. A post-hoc sensitivity protocol, frozen before new training and evaluation, repeats Data, Div, and Full models across three seeds with Tube fixed. Relative to Data, Full reduces primitive composite scores by 26.7 % 26.7\% for Y2 and 26.4 % 26.4\% for Y3 and reduces assembled component-residual and interface-mismatch RMS by 7.2 % 7.2\% and 16.6 % 16.6\% . Nevertheless, mean tree velocity error increases by 7.5 % 7.5\% , and external residual increases from 17.49 ± 4.38 % 17.49\pm 4.38\% to 26.77 ± 3.65 % 26.77\pm 3.65\% . Local regularization can therefore improve primitive and assembled-local diagnostics without ensuring accurate global fields or conservation. Figure 1: (a) Local primitive CFD. (b) Family-specific DeepONets are trained with primitive-level auxiliary constraints and then frozen. (c) Single-pass whole-tree deployment is evaluated against CFD; global conservation is audited, not enforced. 1 Introduction High-fidelity numerical simulation is essential for analysing flow and transport in complex branching systems, but repeatedly solving geometrically detailed domains can be computationally expensive. Learned surrogates amortize this cost by mapping geometries and operating parameters to solution fields. A full-domain surrogate, however, must cover the distribution of complete configurations encountered at inference and offers limited reuse when similar local structures recur across systems. This motivates our central question: can operators learned independently on reusable physical primitives be frozen and composed into an unseen larger system without full-domain retraining? Neural operators provide a natural framework for this question. Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets), Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs), and physics-informed DeepONets learn mappings between input functions or parameterized physical configurations and their solution fields [ 11 , 9 , 15 ] . Geometry-aware extensions such as GINO accommodate varying irregular geometries, but still predict a solution over each complete computational domain [ 10 ] . Generalization across full-domain geometries is therefore distinct from independently learning local component operators and assembling them into a previously unseen hierarchy: the latter additionally requires predictions from different operators to be mutually compatible at their interfaces. Physics-informed objectives can improve local fidelity by incorporating differential-equation residuals, boundary conditions, conservation penalties, and interface or flux constraints [ 15 , 7 ] . These constraints act within the domains on which they are imposed, whereas composition introduces additional system-level requirements. Consequently, low field and physics errors on isolated primitives do not imply a consistent assembled solution: local field accuracy ⇏ globally consistent composition . \text{local field accuracy}\;\not\Rightarrow\;\text{globally consistent composition}. (1) In an incompressible branching system, small component residuals can coexist with parent–child flux mismatches, incompatible pressure gauges, or errors that accumulate across successive generations. Classical Schwarz methods obtain global consistency through iterative transmission of interface information [ 3 ] . Recent learned local-to-global solvers retain explicit coupling: Schwarz Neural Inference and Neural-Schwarz Tiling repeatedly update predictions over overlapping subdomains [ 6 , 14 ] , while CoMLSim combines local representations with iterative inference [ 13 ] . M2PDE instead generates coupled multiphysics or multi-component solutions by sampling from a joint generative model [ 17 ] . We study a deliberately stricter regime: independently trained operators are frozen and evaluated once, then assembled without iterative exchange, joint generation, flux correction, or global projection. The contribution is therefore a controlled composition audit, rather than a converged learned domain-decomposition solver. We investigate this regime using steady two-dimensional airway flow. Airway trees are organized as multigeneration tubular segments connected by branching junctions [ 5 , 8 ] . Following the reusable primitive abstraction developed in RespGeomLib [ 16 ] , we represent these structures as Tube, bifurcation (Y2), and trifurcation (Y3) components, here idealized in two dimensions to permit controlled auditing of component and interface errors. This setting preserves nontrivial velocity, pressure, resistance, and interface physics while allowing component and connection errors to be audited separately. The study is not a patient-specific respiratory model and does not claim unrestricted topology generalization or prediction of physiological terminal-flow redistribution. Here, zero-shot field composition is conditional on a predeclared terminal-flow allocation. Before any monolithic solution field is accessed, each component inflow is obtained from the sum of its descendant terminal flows and determines its parabolic inlet-speed scale; resistance inputs follow the training-row matching rule documented in Appendix A.4 . No assembled tree enters training, validation, selection, or correction, and Selected predictions are frozen before monolithic CFD velocity and pressure fields are inspected. The post-hoc sensitivity audit reuses primitive-selected checkpoints without tree-based selection. We contribute a controlled audit of frozen, single-pass operator composition. The primary validation-selected deployment is archived before whole-tree CFD fields are inspected. A subsequent sensitivity protocol, frozen before new training and evaluation, repeats Data, Div, and Full branching operators over three seeds while holding Tube fixed. The resulting audit separates primitive consistency, assembled component and interface discrepancies, and the external boundary budget. It shows that improvements in the first two levels do not ensure improved global fields or conservation. 2 Method Primitive operators.
